svg.text: TOKEIRA · ARCHITECTURE
The embedded journey
From a durable engine inside your process to a managed cluster — you change the storage line, and nothing else. The execution model never moves.
The part that never changes
let engine = tokeira_engine::Engine::embedded().await?; · ConnectionOptions::service_override(engine.service_override())
The Temporal Rust SDK connects over an in-memory duplex — no TCP, no ports, no daemon. Workflows, activities, signals, timers: the full contract,
with every state change a fenced commit. Storage is a configuration decision underneath it.
THE STORAGE LADDER — EmbeddedStorageConfig, A CLOSED SET
RUNG 1 · THE DEFAULT
In-memory
EmbeddedStorageConfig::InMemory
Ephemeral and instant — tests, examples, day one.
Everything durable-execution about the engine is
already true; only the process boundary is the
blast radius.
restart ⇒ a fresh world
+ A POLICY, NOT A MODE
Snapshots on top
SnapshotPolicyConfig { location, interval_ms }
Restore at boot, capture on a cadence, one final
write on graceful shutdown — the in-memory world
survives restarts. The file is atomically replaced;
the format is versioned and refuses a mismatched
document rather than misreading it.
graceful stop ⇒ nothing lost (the final write)
hard crash ⇒ at most one interval rewound
RUNG 2 · MANAGED
Managed Aurora DSQL
EmbeddedStorageConfig::ManagedDsql(…)
tokeira-managed-dsql owns the cluster lifecycle:
create or recover a dedicated single-Region cluster,
wake it when idle — with a durable creation token so
a crashed first boot never strands or duplicates a
cluster.
restart ⇒ the cluster is found, woken, resumed
RUNG 3 · ADOPTED
Your Aurora DSQL
EmbeddedStorageConfig::ExistingDsql(…)
An operator-supplied cluster, used without lifecycle
mutation — the engine is a guest: it migrates schema
forward-only and never creates, wakes, or destroys.
restart ⇒ reconnect and carry on
What both DSQL rungs get for free
Single-owner exclusion enforced in the database itself — the control lease fences every connection checkout, so a
second engine on the same cluster cannot corrupt it. Connection budgeting runs process-local: no DynamoDB, nothing
to provision. The full 39-table schema, migrated forward-only on first contact.
And when one process stops being enough
The same engine runs as tokeirad — same commit path, same schema, same behaviours the conformance corpus measured.
An embedded DSQL-backed application and a tokeirad fleet are two deployments of one engine, not two systems.
grow into the server; never migrate away from your workflows
The journey's promise:
durability is not a migration event — each rung changes where truth is stored, never what is true or how it is decided.
Companions: the authoritative runtime · embedded (the machinery), the connection reservoir (the DSQL rungs' plumbing), the README's Run Tokeira section.
